deadlineNote: For Master's programmes starting September 2027; late applications not considered.
name: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS)
summary: Tuition contribution of 10,000 to 19,000 EUR for top non-EEA students starting a full-time Master's at Leiden in September. It does not cover all costs.
eligibilityNotes: Page requires a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport; EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland expanded to codes as exclusions. Exception: all nationalities can apply to the Advanced LLM programmes and MSc International Relations and Diplomacy. Award levels are 10,000, 15,000, 17,500, 18,500 or 19,000 EUR, so amount is left empty. Aim for roughly the top 10% of your class.

name: Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship
summary: Full first-year tuition plus a contribution to living costs for excellent international students on a two-year MSc at TU Delft; year two depends on first-year credits. Sixteen awards.
eligibilityNotes: Page says excellent international applicants but gives no nationality list; treated as open to all and the owner should confirm Dutch applicants are out. Aim for about the top 10% of your class. Second year needs at least 48 of 60 ECTS. Amount not on the page.

deadlineNote: Complete MSc application must be submitted before this date.
name: WUR Excellence Programme
summary: Tuition waiver for 24 months for selected students from listed countries starting an on-campus MSc at Wageningen in September 2027. Winners are drawn by lottery from qualified applicants.
eligibilityNotes: Nationalities as listed on the page (21 countries, expanded to codes). People who also hold EU or EFTA nationality are not eligible. Needs unconditional admission and a GPA of 80% or higher. Living costs are not covered; about 16,500 EUR first-year costs must still be paid.

deadlineNote: Complete MSc application must be submitted before this date; September 2027 start.
name: WUR Africa Scholarship Programme (ASP)
summary: Funded MSc at Wageningen for citizens of African countries, covering tuition, a living allowance, travel, visa and insurance for 24 months. Winners are drawn by lottery from qualified applicants.
eligibilityNotes: Page says citizens of an African country with no list; expanded to the 54 recognised African states (Western Sahara not included). Needs a first class degree, GPA 80% or higher, and unconditional admission. Applicants without a Master's are preferred.

deadlineNote: Complete MSc application must be submitted before this date; results expected May 2027.
name: Anne van den Ban Fund (WUR)
summary: Full MSc funding at Wageningen for promising students from listed low-income countries. You cannot apply directly; the fund picks candidates from admitted students.
eligibilityNotes: Citizens of the 63 countries listed on the page, expanded to codes. By invitation only, so students cannot apply directly.

deadlineNote: Differs by institution; check the chosen university.
name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
provider: Dutch Ministry of Education and participating Dutch institutions
summary: A 5,000 EUR contribution for non-EEA students starting a full-time Bachelor's or Master's at a taking part Dutch institution. Each institution sets its own deadlines and programmes.
eligibilityNotes: Page requires non-EEA nationality; EEA states expanded to codes as exclusions. Must not hold a degree from a Dutch institution. Not a full scholarship. Apply via the institution.

deadlineNote: Scholarship form closes 23:59 CET; Master's application must be complete by 10 December 2026.
name: Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship
summary: Full scholarship for non-EU/EEA Master's students at Maastricht, covering tuition and a living payment of 20,150 EUR (one-year Master's) or 38,750 EUR (two-year). Very competitive.
eligibilityNotes: Page excludes EU/EEA, Switzerland and Surinam nationality and EU/EEA/Swiss dual nationals. GPA 7.5 of 10 or higher, age 35 or under on 1 Sept 2027, no earlier degree study in the Netherlands. Living payment differs by programme length, so amount is left empty.

deadlineNote: No direct application; the Master's application must be complete before 1 December and admission offered before February (year not stated on the page).
name: Eric Bleumink Fellowship
summary: Covers tuition, travel, living costs, books and health insurance for MSc, MA or LLM students from listed developing countries. No direct application; Groningen nominates candidates it admits.
eligibilityNotes: Countries of origin as listed on the page, expanded to codes. Selection is by the Admission Office; need excellent grades and no other funding.
